messages:
anya: Noticed a weird 'token smear' in the econ dashboard for model-xyz — tenant A shows a 3x token cost spike around 09:20 but tenant B is flat. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:
sam: Hmm can you paste the query you used to get that?
anya: sure — this is the sample I ran:
```
SELECT model, tenant_id, sum(tokens) AS tok, sum(cost) AS cost
FROM invocation_metrics
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-21T09:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-21T10:00:00Z'
GROUP BY model, tenant_id
ORDER BY tok DESC
```
anya: result shows model-xyz tenant A tok=1.2M cost=$14.3k, tenant B tok=1.1M cost=$4.1k — same token counts but wildly different cost per token.
kevin: :eyes: Could be cache credits being applied differently or a quantization variant routing. Any routing changes around that time?
lia: I pulled cache hit_rate for the same window — tenant A hit_rate drops from 78% -> 22% at 09:18, tenant B stays ~75%.
deploy-bot: [ALERT] cache-metrics-service: high-miss-rate detected for tenant A (svc/cache-watcher) at 2026-03-21T09:18:13Z
sanityCheckId=cc-9f3a
sam: That explains increased raw model tokens, but why cost per token is still higher even after miss -> model fallback? Are we double-counting prefetch credits?
kevin: Possible. We recently changed prefetch attribution smoothing (PR #4821). If sampling rate was low for tenant A, amortization might have assigned credits to a different timebin.
anya: I re-ran the attribution join and noticed the prefetch_credit field is null for many invocations for tenant A. Query:
```
SELECT invocation_id, prefetch_credit, cache_key_hash
FROM invocation_credits
WHERE tenant_id='tenant-A' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-21T09:15:00Z' AND '2026-03-21T09:25:00Z'
LIMIT 20
```
anya: 14/20 rows had prefetch_credit=NULL, but cache_key_hash present.
lia: That implies the credit-lookup service timed out and we defaulted to no credit. The retries service had a backlog then. ops paging @kevin?
kevin: I'm looking at the retry queue — there was a short spike in latency to the crediting API caused by ephemeral redis eviction on the cache-watcher pod. Root cause likely memory OOMs from unrelated batch job.
san: So tenant A got charged full tokens, while tenant B's invocations had credits applied. That creates the 'smear' in per-model cost. Can we proof this with trace ids?
anya: Posted a trace id: trace=trc-7e2b9. Full invocation path shows crediting call timed out 503 at 09:18:12.
kevin: Ok. Short-term mitigation: we should backfill credits for affected window and mark dashboard as adjusted. Long-term: make crediting idempotent and cheap; also add indicator in UI when sampled credits < 95% for a tenant/time window.
lia: Agreed. I'll open an ops runbook PR to add the UI flag and an alert for crediting-sample-rate < 95%.
anya: I'll run a backfill job (low-priority) to recompute credits for tenant A for 09:00-10:00 and post results here.
sam: Can we also add a hover tooltip explaining 'adjusted' vs 'raw' cost? A lot of PMs are going to ask.
kevin: Good call. Let's do: (1) backfill + note on dashboard, (2) alert + UI flag, (3) postmortem linking to PR #4821 hazard. I'll pair with @lia for the alert config.
anya: Backfill job queued: job_id=backfill-20260321-001. I'll update when done.
deploy-bot: [INFO] backfill-20260321-001 started at 2026-03-21T12:05:00Z
anya: update — backfill completed, adjusted tenant A cost down to $4.6k, leaving a small residual diff. Putting a temporary banner on the econ dash with explanation.
sam: Perfect. Thanks team. Can we make a small post in #product and cc billing? They should know why invoices might look odd for that hour.
kevin: Will draft note. Closing loop: assign postmortem to me + lia + anya.
anya: thanks — filing a short postmortem and linking this thread.
